summary: The study describes the use of an ALD-grown Al2O3 interlayer to improve the structural and optical properties of GaN thin films grown on Si(111) substrates. The ALD process significantly reduces strain and dislocation density in the GaN layers, leading to improved material quality compared to GaN grown on bare Si. The ALD-Al2O3 interlayer also helps in reducing crack density and screw dislocation density, making it a promising technique for GaN-based LEDs on Si.
evidence: GaN thin ﬁlms have been grown on Si(111) substrates using an atomic layer deposition (ALD)-grown Al2O3 interlayer. This thin Al2O3 layer reduces strain in the subsequent GaN layer, leading to lower defect densities and improved material quality compared to GaN thin ﬁlms grown by the same process on bare Si. The reduction in strain results in a significant reduction in both crack density and screw dislocation density compared to similar ﬁlms grown on bare Si. Screw dislocation density of the ﬁlms grown on Al2O3/Si substrates approaches that of typical GaN layers on sapphire.
